options_considered: derive from tick per a pre-registered rule
decisions_log.why: The spine has no timestamp column of any kind and never did; the v2 prompt asserted a source without verifying it. Phase 8's det_minute is minute-grain on a seconds-to-minutes quantity and is a post-hoc re-derivation, not scanner output. scanner_hit_catalog.json has a usable timestamp for 3 of 114 cohort events.

decisions_log.chose: centred k-block adaptive kNN evaluated at arrival times
decisions_log.why: Within-session rate spans orders of magnitude, so resolution must follow local density. The centred k-block is the prompt's own 'elapsed time spanning the k nearest prints' made exact and O(n), with no tuning beyond k.

The D7 trigger compares a T=0 price to the T-1 RTH close - a cross-session ratio. flag_cross_session_extreme on the (tm1,t0) pair was joined from the Phase 9 artifact, never re-derived. 6 cohort events flagged; 0 of them never-cross.

Chart 08 is the acceptance gate for row 0. Acceptance is not on the table while four numeric rows have fired; producing it would invert the gate order. Stated in REPORT section 11, not silently skipped.

surprises: About 28% of events have peak arrival intensity BEFORE detection (27.6% at the instantaneous poll, 29.6% at 60s). D6 anticipated this as a first-order finding about the whole program and it is present in this cohort.

Detection segment splits the decay timescale by three orders of magnitude: premarket median decay-to-half 6,693.2s with 0% negative detection-to-peak, versus rth 6.2s with 40% negative. Segment is not an optional conditioning variable on this evidence.

The decay timescale as specified - 'falls to the fraction AND STAYS BELOW for the remainder of the session' - is not well-posed on this data. Per-event values swing across ~10 orders of magnitude as k varies, down to microseconds, because the criterion is decided by whether any later noise spike re-crosses the fraction. That is the mechanism behind failure rows 1 and 6.

Failure row 9 PASSES comfortably (1.010): widening the poll from instantaneous to 60s moves median detection-to-peak by 1.0%. The optimistic bias D7 was written to expose is not material on this cohort - the runway figure is dominated by something other than the polling assumption.
The derived anchor reproduces Phase 8's det_minute on 110/110 events exactly, and the independently recomputed reference price matches tick_close_t_minus_1_rth to 0.000e+00 relative deviation.

Tie handling turned out not to matter at the reference k: median |log ratio| of decay-to-half between tie variants is exactly 0.000 and the peak is identical on 87/100 events. Max tie run is 18, well below k=50.
